findings.problem: The section says three times that Policy 2020-08 cites 105 CMR 700.003(H). That is true of the adopted policy PDF (Adopted 7/31/20, part I). But the mass.gov web page for the same Policy 2020-08 (policy statement dated 05/25/2023) reads 'In accordance with 105 CMR 700.003(J)', and DPH's EPT clinical advisory (updated January 28, 2022) also names 105 CMR 700.003(J) as the governing regulation. The section explains the (J)/(H) mismatch only where it arises in 105 CMR 721.070(A)(7).
findings.rationale: This is not a legal distortion. The policy's substance is the same in both versions, and the PDF the section relies on does cite (H). Orientation[9] already tells the reader that in the current 105 CMR 700.000 expedited partner therapy is in 700.003(H) and that 700.003(J) covers medical device manufacturers, so a candidate can resolve the stale citation wherever it appears. Weighed as Low, and the criterion passes. It is recorded because the same stale (J) cross-reference also appears in the policy's web page and the DPH advisory, not only in 105 CMR 721.070(A)(7).

findings.problem: The section teaches the partner information sheet only as the practitioner's step under 105 CMR 700.003(H)(4). Under its heading for pharmacists, DPH's clinical advisory 'Utilizing Expedited Partner Therapy (EPT) for Chlamydia Infection in Massachusetts' (updated January 28, 2022) says two things. A prescription bearing 'Expedited Partner Therapy,' 'E.P.T.' or 'EPT' in place of a name and address should be filled based on the regulation. And a partner information sheet should be provided whenever possible if the prescriber has not already provided one. The section's pharmacist and pharmacy duties do not mention this guidance step.
findings.rationale: What the section states is accurate. 105 CMR 700.003(H)(4) places counseling and the information sheet on the physician, physician assistant, certified nurse practitioner or nurse midwife. The advisory's sentence for pharmacists is 'should' guidance from a source the section does not declare. The omission would not lead a candidate to a wrong answer about whom 105 CMR 700.003(H)(4) binds; it leaves out an optional step at the pharmacy. Weighed as Low, and the criterion passes.

results.summary: KEEP. Every field was checked against current official texts on 2026-09-16. Contraceptive prescribing: the General Laws page for c. 94C, s. 19F still shows the old subsection (a). St. 2025, c. 14, s. 39 (an emergency law approved August 5, 2025) replaced only subsection (a), and no later 2025-2026 act changing s. 19F, c. 111 s. 121B or c. 118E s. 83 was found. The section treats s. 19F(b)-(c) as directions for the rules and never as duties already in force. As it says, the current 105 CMR 700.004(B)(15) (2/2/2024 text) has no clinical-visit time frame or bar. Circular Letter DCP 26-08-125 (August 25, 2026) matches the section on registration (single pharmacy location), training (before prescribing, five objectives, ACPE/IPCE recommended, documentation upon request), any age, the 12-month ceiling, refills without a clinical visit, the NPI, referral or notification with consent, and the written record. Each guidance item keeps the letter's own modality and is labelled as guidance. Policy 2023-05 with 247 CMR 9.19(1)(f), c. 118E s. 83 and the MassHealth standing order dated January 27, 2025 are stated accurately. Expedited partner therapy: the section correctly states s. 121B as amended by St. 2024, c. 140, ss. 113-114 (effective July 1, 2024), 105 CMR 700.003(H) (chlamydia only; (J) now covers medical device manufacturers), 105 CMR 721.070(A)(7) and (C) and 721.020(D)(4), and Policy 2020-08. That includes profiling and labeling under the designation and referral to an alternate pharmacy by a pharmacist unable or unwilling to fill. The section handles the 721.070(A)(7) citation of 700.003(J) and the conflict between the blank-field allowance and the required name or designation with a sound safe course. DPH's August 2026 guidance on pharmacist STI treatment requires the patient's own laboratory evidence and makes no provision for partner therapy, so the statement that the pharmacist is not the EPT prescriber stands. Practice questions: all ten are answerable from the section and none is contradicted. Two Low observations, neither misleading: the web page for Policy 2020-08 and DPH's 2022 EPT advisory still cite 105 CMR 700.003(J), and the section does not mention the advisory's 'should' step for pharmacists to provide a partner information sheet when the prescriber has not. For context only: 105 CMR 721.070(A)(9) (Schedule VI) and (A)(12) (STI treatment under c. 111, s. 6, whose name and address 721.020(D)(4) also lets be left blank) are further exceptions to electronic prescribing that the section need not teach.
